note: SPAX8 is primarily a central hypomyelinating and spastic ataxia disorder, but peripheral axonal neuropathy has been reported as an atypical or expanding feature in at least two patients.

evidence.text: Bereshneh et al. reported two siblings with SPAX8 who presented with wrist and foot drop due to peripheral axonal neuropathy, expanding the phenotypic spectrum beyond central manifestations.

source.title: Expanding the clinical and neuroimaging features of NKX6-2-related hereditary spastic ataxia type 8
source.quote: In addition, wrist and foot drop due to peripheral axonal neuropathy were observed in these patients as a new clinical finding and cerebellar white matter involvement in brain Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) as new imaging finding.

numbers.metric: affected siblings reported with peripheral neuropathy

evidence.text: The core phenotype across cohorts comprises diffuse central nervous system hypomyelination, early nystagmus, spasticity, and cerebellar ataxia, without typical cavitation or primary dental dysplasia.

source.title: Genetic and phenotypic characterization of NKX6‐2‐related spastic ataxia and hypomyelination
source.quote: NKX6-2 mutations should be considered in patients with autosomal recessive, very early onset of nystagmus, cerebellar ataxia with hypotonia that rapidly progresses to spasticity, particularly when associated with neuroimaging signs of hypomyelination.
